description_en: Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ is located to the southeast of Subāhāḥ (LAL1920) and is separated by a street that runs from east to west. Its classical name is Mayūravarṇa Mahāvihāra. The reason as to why this monastic building was named Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ is disputed, with three main arguments each vying for authority. The first argument claims that the wordbhinchẽis derived from the Sanskrit wordbhinna(meaning "not attached, separated"). The esoteric house of the monastery stands alone, and is not attached to any other building. This argument is supported by an inscription dated NS 789 in Pinchẽ Bāhāḥ which refers to this Bāhāḥ as Bhinnachẽ. Proponents of the second argument point out that an image of Viṣṇu image was found whilst digging for the foundations for esoteric shrine of the monastic building was underway. They argue that this god house was originally namedViṣṇuchẽ, "House of Viṣṇu". Later, the wordViṣṇuchẽchanged into Bhinchẽ. A story in the chronicleNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(12.115) supports this argument. Finally, the third argument puts forward the fact that the daughter of Bandhudatta was married to one of thesaṅghamembers of the Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ. Bandhudatta was one of the priests of King Narendradeva, who was originally from Kathmandu and played a vital role in bringing Matsyendranātha to the Valley. The offspring of Bandhudatta’s daughter used to live in thisbāhāḥ, and while they were resident there people from Kathmandu started to call it Bhinchā Bāhāḥ (abāhāḥof nephews). Bhinchā underwent a sound change and resulted in the modern name Bhinchẽ.The main entry of Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ is to the west and is emphasised by a projectedphalcāattached to a residential building. Thephalcāhas five bays, and the entry passage can be found in the fourth bay from the north. An entry door on the wall of the residential building leads to the courtyard. The central bay of a three-bayedphalcāforms the entry porch, with the other bays on either side of it.A tall, three-tier building can be seen when one stands on the central axis of the entrance and the eastern side. This monument is based on a rectangular plan, sits on a single plinth and is not attached to any other structures. The building is built in such a way that it can be circumambulated. The principal façade is to the west, which has a central door on the ground floor that provides access to the main sanctum room. The rectangular plan of the building has two bays. The rear bay has a colonnaded structure of three bays built with twin pillars. A staircase at the northeastern corner of the building leads the visitor upstairs. A unique feature of this building is its four corner stone pillars on the exterior masonry wall. The front wall of the ground floor is built in grey stone, whilst the southern wall contains images of Vasundharā, Nāmasaṅgīti and Mahākāla. An image of Hanumān is displayed on the northern wall.A goldencaitya-shaped pinnacle tops the monastic building and a goldentoraṇahas been fixed above a carved window on the second floor showing Vajrasattva sitting at its centre. Metal banners containing an image of Māyādevī performingśālabhañjikāhang on either side of this window. A window with a row of five small openings (pāsukājhyāḥ)can be seen on the building's main façade. The frames around the middle opening of the window are gilded while the rest are covered in bronze sheets. Above the window, small statues of the Seven Tathāgatas (Vipaśvī, Śikhī, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa and Śākyamuni), as well as Prajñāpāramitā and Mañjuśrī are displayed. The upper floors have small lattice windows; these have been fitted at the centre of each wall. The pitched overhanging roof is covered with traditionaljhĩgaṭītiles and supported by carved timber struts. The first, third and fourth cornice layers are made of carved timber, while the second level of cornice has a white-plastered dentils pattern and acts as the base of the struts for the first roof. A biggerstūpawith two smallerstūpasform the pinnacle of the temple.The sanctum of the Bāhāḥ is located on the ground floor. Clad in brass, its entry door is flanked by wall paintings of Sāriputra and Maudgalyāyana and topped with a metaltoraṇashowing an image of Dharmadhātuvāgīśvara at its centre with Prajñāpāramitā on the right and Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara on the left. A set of copper plate inscriptions, stone inscriptions and metal flags can be found on either side of the door. Inside the sanctum, a metal image of Akṣobhya serves as the main deity of the Bāhāḥ. A short stone pillar rises out of the second-last step and is topped with a metalvajra. A pillar of Aparamitā can be found to the north of these steps, whilst a pillar of Prajñāpāramitā is located to the south. The four corners of the esoteric building house images of a leopard (southeast), an elephant (southwest), an immortal man (northwest) and a lion (northeast).The courtyard is paved in telia tiles and measures 18.8 m x 17.7 m. It contains aśikharakūṭoparipadma caitya, twośikharakūṭa caityas, astūpapillar, a lotus pillar and adharmadhātu maṇḍala,all of which are arranged in a line in front of the temple. The esoteric deity (āgãdyaḥ) is kept in thedigīhouse. This is located on the eastern side of the adjacent large courtyard, alongside a number ofstūpasand small shrines.No historical evidence could be found to confirm when exactly this monastic building was constructed. According to the chronicleNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(12.115), Jayaśrī built this monastery during the reign of King Śaṅkaradeva (son of Vṛṣadeva). The chronicle further tells that Jayaśrī decried the doctrines of Śaṅkarasvāmī (probably Śaṅkarācārya) before heading to Cārumatī Vihāra marrying a Bhikṣu’s daughter. Later, he decided to build a monastic building. Whilst he was preparing to build thevihāra, he and other Bhikṣus were struggling to work out where it should be constructed when they suddenly saw a peacock land. Thy dug up the place where the bird landed and found an image of Viṣṇu. They then established an image of Lord Śākyasiṃha at that place. For this reason, thevihārawas named Mayūravarṇaviṣṇukṣa Vihāra. This legend suggests that this monastic building was established in the Licchavi period. However, no historical evidence has been found to support this claim. The earliest mention of this monastic building can be found in a palm-leaf manuscript dated NS 550 (CE 1430) which was found in Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra (Śākya1973, 16).Śākya(1980, 13) has surmised that the Busĩchẽ Vihāra mentioned in one of the palm-leaf manuscript dated NS 261 (CE 1141) might be the modern Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ.
description_ne: यो बाहा: ललितपुरको पूर्व दिशामा पर्छ । यसको संस्कृत नाम मयूरवर्ण महाविहार हो । यो बाहा:को नाम भिन्छेँ बाहा: किन भयो भन्नेबारे तीनथरी मत छन्: १. यो बाहा:को द्य:छेँ दायाँ-बायाँ अन्य कुनै संरचनासँग नजोडिई अलग उभिएको छ । कतै नजोडिई उभिएकोले यो बाहा:को नाम भिन्छेँ बाहा: भएको हो । पिन्छेँ बाहा: (LAL2050) को नेसं ७८९ को अभिलेखमा यो बाहा:लाई भिन्नछे बाहा: भनी लेखिएको छ । २. यो बाहा: निर्माण गर्न जग खन्दा विष्णुको मूर्ति भेटिएको थियो । विष्णुको मूर्ति भेटिएको बाहा: हुनाले विष्णुछेँबाहा: हुँदै भिन्छेँबाहा: भएको हो । ३. यो बाहा:मा रहेका संघ-सदस्यहरूमध्ये केहीको सम्बन्ध रातो मत्स्येन्द्रनाथसँग जोडिएको छ । रातो मत्स्येन्द्रनाथलाई काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा ल्याउने व्यक्तिहरूमध्ये एक काठमाडौंका बन्धुदत्त आचार्य पनि हुन् । तिनै बन्धुदत्त आचार्यकी एक छोरीको विवाह भिन्छेँबाहा:का एक संघ-सदस्यसँग भएको थियो । बन्धुदत्त आचार्यकी छोरीबाट जन्म भएका सन्तान बस्ने बाहा:लाई काठमाडौंका मानिसले भिन्चा बाहा: (भान्जाको बाहा:) भन्न थाले । त्यसै भिन्चा बाहा: शब्दको ध्वनि परिवर्तन भएर पछि भिन्छेँ बाहा: भएको हो ।ललितपुरको स:को-सुबाहा: टोलबाट पूर्व गएपछि दक्षिणमा एउटा ढोका देखिन्छ । उक्त ढोकाबाट भित्र गएपछि पूर्वमा भिन्छेबाहा: प्रवेश गर्ने मूल प्रवेशद्वार भेटिन्छ । मूल प्रवेशद्वारमा छिर्नुभन्दा अघि ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ फल्चा बनाइएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारको उत्तरमा ४ कवलको र दक्षिणमा १ कवलको फल्चा बनाइएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारबाट भित्र छिरेपछि पनि दायाँ-बायाँ भजन गर्न फल्चा बनाइएका छन् । मूल प्रवेशद्वारको ठीक सामुन्ने पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी तीन तहको छानायुक्त पाँच तल्ले द्य:छेँ रहेको छ । अन्य बाहा:को द्य:छेँभन्दा यस बाहा:को द्य:छेँ फरक छ । अरु बाहा:को द्य:छेँ दायाँ-बायाँ अन्य संरचनासँग जोडिएर बनाइएको हुन्छ । तर भिन्छेँबाहा:को द्य:छेँ दायाँ-बायाँ नजोडीकन स्वतन्त्र रूपले उभिएको छ । तीनै तहको छानालाई अड्याउन कलात्मक टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । द्य:छेँको सबभन्दा माथि गजूरको रूपमा सुवर्ण चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । गजूरदेखि द्य:छेँको पहिलो तल्लासम्म पुग्ने गरी पता: झुण्ड्याइएको छ । द्य:छेँको दोस्रो तल्लाको बीचमा कलात्मक झ्याल बनाई सुवर्ण तोरण सहित वज्रसत्व स्थापना गरिएको छ । उक्त झ्यालको दायाँ-बायाँ धातुको पातामा सालभञ्जिका मुद्रामा मायादेवी अंकित गरिएको छ । पहिलो तल्लामा पासुखाझ्याल राखिएको छ । पासुखाझ्यालका पाँच झ्यालमध्ये बीचको झ्यालमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छ भने अन्य चारवटा झ्यालमा पित्तलले मोडिएको छ । पासुखाझ्यामाथि सप्ततथागत (विपश्वी, शिखि, विश्वभू, क्रकुच्छन्द, कनकमुनि, काश्यप, शाक्यमुनि), प्रज्ञापारमिता र मञ्जुश्री गरी नौजना देवताको मूर्ति राखिएको छ । भुइँतल्लामा बाहा:को गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकामाथि धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । तोरणको मध्यभागमा धर्मधातुवागीश्वर राखिएको छ भने दायाँतिर प्रज्ञापारमिता र बायाँतिर षडक्षरी लोकेश्वर राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र अक्षोभ्य बुद्धलाई क्वा:पा:द्य:को रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने द्वारको दायाँ-बायाँ धातुको सारिपुत्र-मौदगल्यायनको मूर्ति र धातुको झण्डा राखिएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारको दायाँ-बायाँ शिलापत्र र ताम्रपत्रहरू राखिएका छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र जान बनाइएको सिँढीको दायाँ-बायाँ ढुंगाका सिंह र धातुको घण्टा राखिएका छन् । सिँढीमा नै शिलास्तम्भनाथि धातुको वज्र राखिएको छ । सिँढीको उत्तरमा अपरमिता र दक्षिणमा प्रज्ञापारमिताको स्तम्भ बनाइएको छ । बाहा:को प्राङ्गनमा चैत्य, धर्मधातु, स्तम्भ स्थापना गरिएका छन् । बाहा:को चार कुनामा चार कृति स्थापना गरिएको छ । दक्षिण-पूर्वमा शार्दूल, दक्षिण-पश्चिममा हात्ती, उत्तर-पश्चिममा अजरामरपुरुष र पूर्व-उत्तरमा सिंह स्थापना गरिएको छ । द्य:छेँ बाहेक चारैतिर आवासीय घरहरू रहेका छन् । द्य:छेँको पूर्वमा भिन्छेँबाहा: ननि रहेको छ भने ननिको पूर्वमा भिन्छेँबाहा:को दिगि रहेको छ । उक्त दिगिमा नै भिन्छेबाहा:को आगम पनि रहेको छ ।यो बाहा: कहिले बन्यो भन्ने स्पष्ट पार्ने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण भेटिएको छैन । किंवदन्तीअनुसार लिच्छवि राजा वृषदेवका छोरा शंकरदेवको पालामा जयश्री नामका ब्राह्मणले यो बाहा: बनाएका हुन् । जयश्रीले शंकराचार्यको सिद्धान्तलाई अस्वीकार गरी चारुमती विहारमा गई बौद्ध भिक्षुहरूको संगत गरी बुद्धधर्ममा दीक्षित भइसकेपछि विहार बनाउने इच्छा गरे । तर कुन ठाउँमा बनाउने बनी सरसल्लाह गरिरहँदा अकस्मात् एउटा मयूर आकाशमार्गबाट उडेर आई एक ठाउँमा बस्यो । मयूर बसेको ठाउँमा विहार बनाएपछि मयूरवर्ण महाविहार भन्ने नाम रहन गयो । विहारको जग खन्दा विष्णुको मूर्ति भेट्टिएकोले विष्णुछेँबाहा: भन्न थालियो (Wright 1877,123-124). किंवदन्तीमा लिच्छविकालमा बनाइएको भनिएपनि लिच्छविकालको विहार भनी प्रमाणित गर्ने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण भेटिँदैन । यो विहारको नाम उल्लेख गरिएको अहिलेसम्म प्राप्त सबैभन्दा पुरानो प्रमाण हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहारमा भेटिएको नेसं ५५० को ताडपत्र हो (Śākya 1973, 16) । रुद्रवर्ण महाविहारमा भेटिएको नेसं २६१ को ताडपत्रमा उल्लेख गरिएको बुसिंछेँ विहार (Śākya 1980, 13) आजभोलिको भिन्छेँबाहा: हुनसक्छ । यसबारे थप अध्ययनको आवश्यकता छ ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: Sources and references Sources Inscription on Maṇḍala

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a maṇḍala
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records that a certain Pūnajoti offered a brass wrappedmaṇḍalawhich is kept in front of the entrance to Kvāpāḥdyaḥ.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of utensils for daily worship
historical_events.event_description: Utensils for daily worship were donated by Devarāja, Dharmaśrī, Mahāmuni and others.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a golden tree to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
historical_events.event_description: A golden tree was donated to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ. On that occasion a gold bracelet was also donated to Cakrasaṃvara Vajravārāhī and was placed inside theāgamaby Devarāja, Dharmarāja, Mahāmuni and others.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of golden Ilā̃ to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
historical_events.event_description: A goldenIlā̃was donated to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a gilded crown to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
historical_events.event_description: A gilded crown was donated to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥby Lājabira Sĩ (Rājabīra Singh).

historical_events.event_name: The earliest mention of Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ
historical_events.event_description: Bhinchẽ Bāhāḥ is mentioned asViṣṇuchẽ Bāhārāin this palm-leaf deed.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of dyaḥchẽ
historical_events.event_description: Thedyaḥchẽof Mayūravarṇa Mahāvihāra was renovated.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of khasi (jambs)
historical_events.event_description: Door jambs (khasi) were donated on the either side of entrance to sanctum by Budhadeva, Śikṣamuni and Indrajoti.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a triratna statue
historical_events.event_description: Dharmarāya Vajrācārya donated a statue oftriratna(Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha) during the reign of King Mahendra Siṃha (Bhāṣkara Malla).

historical_events.event_name: Donation for gilding the Akṣobhya statue
historical_events.event_description: Dhanaratna, Dharmadeva, Puṇyalāya and others donated funds to gild the Akṣobhya image.

historical_events.event_name: Donation for the pavement of the courtyard
historical_events.event_description: Gunasali donated funds for the courtyard of thebāhāḥto be paved withteliabricks.

historical_events.event_name: Cladding the entrance door to the sanctum
historical_events.event_description: Padmānanda and his family clad the entrance door to the sanctum in brass plates.

historical_events.event_name: Donation for the main door and for gilding the toraṇa above the entrance to the sanctum
historical_events.event_description: The name of the main donor is illegible but the members of the donor's family can still be made out. They read as follows: Pūrṇarāja, Tejarāja, Harṣarāja, Dharmarāja, Vasundharā. Thetoraṇaabove the entrance of the sanctum was gilded.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the roof of the esoteric building
historical_events.event_description: The roof of the esoteric building was repaired. The spirits of the the gods were returned to the temple through thedaśakarmaritual. Allsaṅghamembers were involved in this event.

historical_events.event_name: Gilding the middle opening of the pāsukā jhyālaand covereing other openingswith bronze plates
historical_events.event_description: In memory of his late father Harṣapati, Tejabīra gilded the middle opening of thepāsukā jhyālaand covered other openings with bronze plates. This took place during the reign of King Pṛthvīvīravikrama Śāha.

historical_events.event_name: Replacement of the wooden bell stand with a stone one
historical_events.event_description: The old wooden bell stand was replaced with a stone bell stand. A new chain for the bell was also donated by Lakṣmibila (Lakṣmībīra) Vajrācārya, Sīgha Joti and Bhīmanarasī.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of Aparamitā and Prajñāpāramitā statues
historical_events.event_description: Dharmarāja Śākya and his wife Lakṣmīmāyā installed statues of Aparamitā and Prajñāpāramitā.

historical_events.event_name: Erection of a stone pillar
historical_events.event_description: In memory of their father Bhimarāja, mother Lāni Thakuṃ and elder son, Dharmaratna Harmarāja and his wife Lakṣmīmāyā erected a stone pillar (LAL2060-006) in thebāhāḥcourtyard.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of a śikharakūṭa caitya
historical_events.event_description: Āsāmadu Vajrācārya, his wife Lachi(mi)māyā, and their two daughters Budhamāyā and Budhalakṣimi made a newśikharakūṭa caityato cover the damagedaśoka caitya.

historical_events.event_name: Erection of a pillar
historical_events.event_description: Tejabīra erected a pillar (LAL2060-006) in thebāhāḥcourtyard. This is used to offerpiṇḍa.

historical_events.event_name: Reconstruction of the esoteric shrine
historical_events.event_description: Thesaṅgha-members ofbāhāḥreconstructed the esoteric shrine of the monastic building after it collapsed in the 1934 earthquake.

historical_events.event_name: Gilding the image of Akṣobhya
historical_events.event_description: Under the leadership of Tīrtharāja, the members of thesaṅghaundertook a pilgrimage in which they collected funds and donations in NS 1071. Later, in NS 1074, they used this money to gild the image of Akṣobhya.

historical_events.event_name: Destruction of Bāhāḥ by earthquake
historical_events.event_description: Thebāhāḥwas completely demolished in the 1934 earthquake.

historical_events.event_name: Support of the government for the renovation of the esoteric shrine
historical_events.event_description: The Government of Nepal supported local people in repairing the esoteric shrine during the reign of King Vīrendra.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of golden a toraṇa
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records that Yaṃdrajati, Hākudeva, Sujadeva and other jointly offered a gold-platedtoraṇato the Bāhāḥ.
